test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Kalpana and Sudha got 621 and 522 marks, respectively, in the same examination. If Kalpana scored 69% marks, then what is the percentage of marks scored by Sudha?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Compare marks directly with percentages since the **Maximum Marks** are the same.

621 marks → 69%

1 mark → 69 ÷ 621 %

522 marks → (69 ÷ 621) × 522 %

522 marks → (1 ÷ 9) × 522 = 58%

**∴ The correct answer is 58%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Marks of **Kalpana** = 621, Percentage of **Kalpana** = 69%, Marks of **Sudha** = 522.

**Formula Used:** Maximum Marks = (Obtained Marks ÷ Percentage) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50c637f26e33c25eb20779c8d80004bcef168a25663e6c76dadad39232bd33a0.png] 

⇒ Let the **Maximum Marks** be M.

⇒ 69% of M = 621

⇒ (69 ÷ 100) × M = 621

⇒ M = (621 × 100) ÷ 69 = 900

⇒ **Sudha's Percentage** = (Marks Scored ÷ Maximum Marks) × 100

⇒ Percentage = (522 ÷ 900) × 100

⇒ Percentage = 522 ÷ 9 = 58%

**∴ The correct answer is 58%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

Percentage change = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100. Useful for comparing growth or decline.

Passing Marks Concept

Passing Marks = Total Marks × Passing Percentage. Often used in exam-based word problems.

Base Value consistency

When the base (Total Marks) is the same, values and percentages are **directly proportional**.</p
